title: Potato and Cauliflower Bake
subtitle: with Smoked Cheddar and Blistered Beans
description: You may notice this recipe's back for a victory lap – that's because sometimes you can't beat a tried-and-true winner! Our Dinnerly home cooks loved this recipe, so here it is again for you to enjoy its easy cooking, big flavours and satisfying goodness.

steps.text: Parboil veggies: Preheat the oven to 220C. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil. Cut the unpeeled potatoes into 5mm-thick rounds. Cut the cauliflower stem into 1cm chunks, then cut the head into small florets (see Kitchen 101). Cook the potato and cauliflower in the pan of boiling water for 5 mins or until just tender. Drain. Wipe the pan clean and reserve.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, trim the beans. Finely chop the rosemary leaves, discarding the stems. Coarsely grate the cheese. Put the rosemary and half the cheese in a bowl. Add 5g butter and rub the mixture with your fingertips until combined. Put the country seasoning in a heatproof jug, add 60ml (¼ cup) milk and 180ml (¾ cup) boiling water and stir to dissolve.

Make sauce: Heat 10g butter and 1 tbs olive oil in the reserved pan over medium heat. Add 1 tbs plain flour and cook, stirring, for 2-3 mins until golden. Reduce the heat to low and gradually whisk in the milk mixture. Cook, stirring, for 2-3 mins until thickened. Add the remaining cheese and stir until smooth. Remove the pan from the heat.

Cook potato bake: Put the cauliflower in a 1.5L (6 cup) baking dish. Arrange the potato over the top, overlapping the slices. Pour over the sauce and scatter over the cheese mixture. Bake on the upper oven shelf for 15 mins or until bubbling and golden. Meanwhile, put the beans and almonds on the lined tray. Drizzle with 1 tsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat.

Serve up: Bake the beans and almonds on the lower shelf for 6 mins or until the almonds are toasted and the beans are tender but still with crunch. Drizzle with 1 tsp balsamic vinegar and toss to combine. Divide the potato and cauliflower bake among plates. Serve with the beans and almonds and enjoy!
Kitchen 101: Once you remove the centre stem from the cauliflower, it will naturally fall apart into large florets. You can then use your knife to break these down into smaller, bite-sized florets.
